easy.def: To hold someone close in your arms.
examples: I hug my mom.
Grandma hugged me.
The kids hugged the puppy.

more.def: To put your arms around someone and hold them tight to show love.
examples: She hugged her friend goodbye at the bus stop.
The children hugged each other after the show.
He hugged his teddy bear tightly.

easy.def: A tight hold with your arms around someone.
examples: I gave Dad a hug.
A hug feels warm.
Grandma gave me a big hug.

more.def: The act of holding someone close in your arms to show love.
examples: A warm hug made me feel better.
He gave his sister a big hug at the airport.
Everyone got a hug at the family party.
A whale is huge.
We saw a huge truck.
I have a huge smile today.

more.def: Extremely large in size or amount.
examples: A huge crowd gathered to watch the parade.
The storm left a huge puddle in the yard.
Winning the award was a huge surprise.

easy.def: To sing with your lips closed.
examples: I hum a song.
She hummed while she worked.
Dad hums a tune.

more.def: To make a low, steady sound, or to sing a tune without opening your mouth.
examples: I hummed a tune as I walked.
The bees hummed in the garden.
The refrigerator hums in the kitchen.
Humans have two legs.
A human can use tools.
Dogs are friends of humans.

more.def: A person; a member of the kind of living thing that people belong to.
examples: Humans have been making tools for thousands of years.
The robot looked almost like a human.
Dolphins and humans can both learn from others.
The human body needs water.
Eating is a human need.
A human heart beats all day.

more.def: Of or belonging to people.
examples: Sleeping is a basic human need.
The museum has a model of the human heart.
It is only human to make mistakes.
Humanity needs clean water.
The invention helped humanity.
We are all part of humanity.

more.def: All the people of the world, or kindness toward others.
examples: Clean water is important to all of humanity.
The doctor showed great humanity.
The scientist hoped to help humanity.
The winner was humble and kind.
She is humble about her good grades.
The humble boy did not show off.

more.def: Not thinking or acting as if you are better than other people.
examples: Even after winning the prize, she stayed humble.
The humble champion thanked his teammates first.
He gave a humble answer when people praised his work.

easy.def: To make someone feel very small and ashamed.
examples: Do not humiliate people.
She felt humiliated.
He humiliated her in front of the class.

more.def: To make someone feel foolish or ashamed in front of others.
examples: It is cruel to humiliate someone in front of others.
He felt humiliated when everyone laughed at his mistake.
The boy was humiliated by the mean joke.
He has a good sense of humor.
The book is full of humor.
I like her humor.

more.def: The quality of being funny, or the ability to see what is funny.
examples: He has a great sense of humor.
The story is full of humor.
A little humor made the lesson fun.
The camel has a hump.
The road has a hump.
The hump is big.

more.def: A round bump on the back of an animal or on the ground.
examples: The camel's hump stores fat.
The car bumped over a hump in the road.
A whale showed its hump above the water.

easy.def: A feeling that something is true without proof.
examples: I have a hunch it will rain.
His hunch was right.
She had a hunch.

more.def: A feeling that you have about something even though you have no proof.
examples: I have a hunch that it will rain tomorrow.
His hunch was right, and he found the key.
She followed her hunch and looked under the bed.

easy.def: To bend your back and shoulders forward.
examples: He hunched over the desk.
She hunched in the cold.
The old man hunched.

more.def: To bend your back and shoulders forward and round.
examples: He hunched over the desk to write.
She hunched her shoulders against the wind.
The cat hunched up in the rain.
Count to one hundred.
A hundred kids came to the fair.
She is a hundred years old.

more.def: The number 100, which is ten tens.
examples: A dollar is a hundred cents.
Hundreds of people watched the parade.
The tree is over a hundred years old.
I am hungry for lunch.
The hungry baby cried.
Are you hungry for a snack?

more.def: Feeling that you need or want to eat.
examples: The hungry kittens meowed until they were fed.
After the long hike, we were all hungry.
The hungry birds gathered at the feeder.
We hunt for shells.
She hunted for her shoe.
I hunt for eggs.

more.def: To search for something.
examples: We hunted for seashells on the beach.
She hunted for her missing shoe.
The kids hunt for eggs at Easter.

easy.def: To chase and catch animals for food.
examples: Owls hunt at night.
Lions hunt for food.
Wolves hunt in packs.

more.def: To chase and kill wild animals for food or sport.
examples: Owls hunt mice at night.
Lions hunt together to catch zebras.
Long ago, people hunted to feed their families.

easy.def: Looking for animals to catch for food.
examples: Wolves go hunting at night.
The owl does its hunting after dark.
Cats like hunting.

more.def: The act of looking for and catching animals for food.
examples: Wolves do their hunting at night.
The eagle spotted a mouse while hunting.
Long ago, people lived by hunting and gathering.

easy.def: A very big storm with strong wind and lots of rain.
examples: The hurricane knocked down trees.
We stayed inside in the hurricane.
A hurricane brings big waves.

more.def: A huge, powerful storm with very strong winds and heavy rain that forms over the ocean.
examples: People boarded up their windows before the hurricane arrived.
The hurricane flooded streets near the coast.
Weather experts tracked the hurricane as it crossed the sea.

easy.def: To move or do something fast.
examples: Hurry, or we will be late!
I hurried to the door.
We hurry to catch the bus.

more.def: To move or act quickly because there is not much time.
examples: We hurried to the station so we would not miss the train.
Hurry up, or the ice cream will melt!
She hurried through her homework so she could go outside.
I am in a hurry.
Why are you in such a hurry?
Dad was in a hurry.

more.def: A need to do something quickly because time is short.
examples: In her hurry, she forgot her lunch box.
There is no hurry, so take your time.
He ran out the door in a hurry.
My knee hurts.
I hurt my arm.
Do not hurt the cat.

more.def: To cause pain or an injury, or to feel pain.
examples: I fell and hurt my knee on the pavement.
Does your tooth still hurt?
Her words hurt his feelings.
I am hurt.
The hurt dog limps.
She felt hurt.

more.def: Feeling pain in the body, or feeling upset.
examples: The hurt bird could not fly until its wing healed.
He felt hurt when his friend forgot his birthday.
The nurse helped the hurt child.

easy.def: A man who is married to someone.
examples: Aunt Rosa's husband drives a bus.
Her husband bakes bread on Sundays.
Is he your friend's husband?

more.def: A married man, when you are talking about the person he is married to.
examples: The author thanked her husband for reading her stories first.
The two sisters and their husbands went camping together.
My neighbor and her husband planted a big vegetable garden.
Hush, the baby is asleep.
She hushed the crowd.
The class hushed.

more.def: To make someone be quiet, or to become quiet.
examples: Hush, the baby is sleeping.
The teacher hushed the class.
The crowd hushed as the show began.
We hustle to the bus.
The kids hustled to class.
Hustle up!

more.def: To move or work quickly.
examples: The kids hustled to catch the bus.
He hustled down the hall.
Hustle up, or we will be late.
The hut is made of mud.
They lived in a hut.
The hut has one room.

more.def: A very small, plain house, often made from wood, mud or grass.
examples: The hut had a roof made of grass.
The shepherd slept in a hut.
We built a hut in the woods.
